newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Holiday couple scores big with aircrash video.
newsitem.headline: Holiday couple scores big with aircrash video.

text.p: A South African couple who made a video recording of the crash of a hijacked Ethiopian Airlines plane sold the film for $87,000, South African newspapers reported on Wednesday.
Marinda and Dolf Gouws of Pretoria were on honeymoon at a beach hotel in the Comoros Islands when the Boeing 767 plunged into the sea before their eyes, killing 125 people.
Marinda, 23, filmed the entire sequence including limbless bodies being dragged from the water.

Their cassette was bought by Worldwide Television News (WTN) for 400,000 South African rand, the highest bidder among television news organisations covering the aftermath of the crash, which 50 passengers and crew survived.
"Although we made a great deal of money from the crash, we were really upset about it and felt terrible for the people who were killed," Marinda Gouws was quoted as saying.
